items.title: What I Learned from Evaluating a Scientific AI Agent
items.why: A practitioner's account of evaluating a scientific agent when there is no single right answer. It splits evaluation into tool execution, tool selection, scientific interpretation and multi-step workflows. It is one author's experience on one antibody-optimisation project, not a benchmark result.
items.takeaway: Use deterministic checks wherever possible, and version prompts, tools and workflow instructions alongside reported scores.

items.title: Structural Basis for Human Milk Oligosaccharides Recognition by Evolutionarily Dominant Norovirus Genogroup II Genotypes
items.by: Pisapia, L.; Flatau, H. N.; Lin, S.; Calamandrei, R.; Cerofolini, L.; Munoz-Garcia, J. C.; Imberty, A.; Fragai, M.; Angulo, J.; Varrot, A.
items.why: A structural-biology preprint (not peer reviewed) that combines NMR and X-ray crystallography to study how fucosylated human milk oligosaccharides bind norovirus P domains. It covers weak, rapidly exchanging interactions and genotype-specific binding surfaces, and is a good example of how binding methods complement each other.
items.takeaway: The abstract reports fucose anchoring through five conserved residues, with GII.4 driven mainly by hydrogen bonds and GII.17 relying more on water-mediated interactions.

items.title: On the Role of Theory in Biology
items.why: A long essay on the history of theory in biology, from Borelli and D'Arcy Thompson to Rashevsky and McCulloch–Pitts. It is conceptual breadth beyond the usual feed, useful for thinking about what models in biology are for.
items.takeaway: The author argues that theory has played a generative role in biological discovery, not just a role in summarising data.

items.title: The geometry of diffusion guidance
items.why: A geometric picture of diffusion sampling and classifier and classifier-free guidance, with an explicit warning about 2D intuition in high dimensions.
items.takeaway: Guidance adds a scaled conditioning direction to the model's sampling update.

items.title: Reward Hacking in Reinforcement Learning
items.why: A survey of reward hacking and specification gaming in RL and RLHF that connects Goodhart's law to concrete examples. It complements the fresh agent-evaluation post on how proxy metrics mislead.
items.takeaway: The author argues that any proxy reward can be exploited and calls for more research on practical mitigations.

items.title: Understanding Convolutions on Graphs
items.why: A careful, visual build-up of graph neural networks from the graph Laplacian and polynomial filters, with molecules as a motivating example. It is useful background for molecular and protein modelling.
items.takeaway: It frames node-order equivariance and locality as the core design constraints on graph convolutions.

items.title: Visualizing Weights
items.why: An interpretability article on making sense of weights between hidden layers, using factorisation and feature visualisation for context. It offers a different angle on understanding learned mechanisms, with an explicit analogy to neuroscience connectomes.
items.takeaway: The article argues that weights between hidden layers are meaningless without context, which feature visualisation can supply.

items.title: Understanding LSTM Networks
items.why: A classic, clear step-by-step explanation of LSTM gating and the cell state.
items.takeaway: The cell state works like a conveyor belt, and gates regulate what is removed or added.

earlier.title: A novel mechanism for morphological change during bacterial sporulation based on programmed peptidoglycan degradation
earlier.why: Peer-reviewed cell-biology paper on how Myxococcus xanthus remodels its cell wall during sporulation, which does not use cell division. It covers two lytic transglycosylases and a mechanism of programmed peptidoglycan degradation, and the eLife assessment rates the evidence as solid.
earlier.takeaway: The two lytic transglycosylases LtgA and LtgB are required for sporulation, and LtgB sets the pace of LtgA-driven peptidoglycan degradation.

earlier.title: Noise schedules considered harmful
earlier.why: An opinionated explanation of why noise schedules in diffusion models may confuse more than they clarify.
earlier.takeaway: It argues for reframing diffusion around which noise levels matter, using perceptual relevance and learning difficulty, instead of around the schedule itself.

earlier.title: RL without TD learning
earlier.why: A Berkeley blog post on a divide-and-conquer alternative to temporal-difference value learning for off-policy RL. It adds optimization breadth beyond generative modelling. The results are the authors' own, and the post says the method is so far limited to goal-conditioned RL with deterministic dynamics.
earlier.takeaway: Transitive RL updates values by combining two sub-trajectory values, which lets it match the best tuned n-step TD without choosing n.
